record.title: Guenda et al.'s conjecture on linear intersection pairs of codes
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $[n,k_1,d_1]_q$ and $[n,k_2,d_2]_q$ denote $q$-ary linear codes of length $n$, dimensions $k_1,k_2$, and minimum distances $d_1,d_2$. Two codes form a **linear $\ell$-intersection pair** when the dimension of their intersection is $\ell$.

**Guenda et al.'s conjecture.** Provided that $[n,k_1,d_1]_q$ and $[n,k_2,d_2]_q$ codes exist, there exists a linear $\ell$-intersection pair of such codes for every integer $\ell$ satisfying

$$
k_1+k_2-n\leq \ell\leq \min\{k_1,k_2\}.
$$

The lower bound is forced by the dimension formula for the intersection of two length-$n$ codes, while the upper bound is immediate from the two dimensions. The conjecture asks whether every admissible intersection dimension can always be realized while preserving the specified code parameters; the supplied text does not report a resolution.

record.title: Steiner-system extremal conjecture for constant-column-weight disjunct matrices
record.statement:
Let $M$ be an $n\times m$ $t$-disjunct matrix with constant column weight $b$. Set

$$
p=\frac{b+t-1}{t},
$$

and assume that $p$ is an integer. A Steiner system $\mathfrak{S}(n,b,p)$ is a family of $b$-subsets of an $n$-element set such that every $p$-subset is contained in exactly one member; the maximum such family is denoted by $\mathfrak{S}(n,b,p)$. **Steiner-system conjecture.** The maximum $\mathfrak{S}(n,b,p)$ Steiner system gives a matrix $M'$ that is no worse than $M$, equivalently,

$$
|\mathfrak{S}(n,b,p)|\ge m.
$$

The conjecture proposes that Steiner-system constructions are at least as efficient as arbitrary constant-column-weight $t$-disjunct matrices with the same parameters. The surrounding discussion notes that the Steiner construction yields a $\left\lfloor\frac{b-1}{p-1}\right\rfloor$-disjunct matrix, but the supplied text gives no resolution of this conjecture.

record.title: The simplicial freeness conjecture for the Brunnian planar braid subgroup
record.statement:
Let $SPT_*$ be the simplicial group of simplicial pure twin groups, let $c_{111}$ be the 2-simplex with trivial faces, and let $K_*$ be the smallest simplicial subgroup of $SPT_*$ containing $c_{111}$. Let $S^2$ be the simplicial sphere with non-degenerate 2-simplex $\sigma=(0,1,2)$, and let $F[S^2]_*$ be Milnor's free simplicial group on $S^2$. The simplicial homomorphism

$$
\Theta:F[S^2]_*\longrightarrow K_*
$$

is induced by the simplicial map sending $\sigma$ to $c_{111}$. **The simplicial freeness conjecture.** The homomorphism

$$
\Theta:F[S^2]_*\longrightarrow K_*
$$

is an isomorphism. This would identify the simplicial subgroup generated by $c_{111}$ with Milnor's free simplicial group on the simplicial 2-sphere, extending the verified injectivity in degrees at most $4$ and providing a description of the homotopy groups of $S^3$ through the Moore complex of $K_*$.

record.title: Conjecture on the zeros of the Mittag–Leffler function with second parameter 2
record.statement:
Let $E_{\alpha,\beta}$ denote the Mittag–Leffler function. There exists some $\alpha_0\in(1.59911,1.59912)$, and for $\alpha\geq\alpha_0$ let $Z_2(\alpha)$ denote the smallest positive solution of $E_{\alpha,2}(-z^\alpha)=0$.

**Smallest-zero conjecture for $E_{\alpha,2}$.** For each $\alpha\in[\alpha_0,2]$, the equation

$$
E_{\alpha,2}(-z^\alpha)=0
$$

has at least one solution in $(0,\infty)$. As $\alpha\to2-$,

$$
Z_2(\alpha)=\pi+(2-\alpha)+o(2-\alpha),
$$

and as $\alpha\to\alpha_0+$,

$$
Z_2(\alpha)=Z_2(\alpha_0)+c(\alpha-\alpha_0)^b(1+o(1)),
$$

where $Z_2(\alpha_0)\approx5.21066$, $b\approx1/2$, and $c\approx-4.8$. Furthermore, $Z_2(\alpha)$ is strictly decreasing in $\alpha$. For each $\alpha\in(1,\alpha_0)$, $E_{\alpha,2}(-z^\alpha)>0$ for all $z\geq0$.

The threshold and the asserted behavior are based on numerical observations; the exact value of $\alpha_0$ and the stated asymptotics and monotonicity remain unproved here. The context attributes the existence of a threshold to earlier work but does not establish these precise claims.

record.title: Conjecture on the Cantor–Bendixson structure of spaces of shifts
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}^d$ denote the space of $d$-dimensional shifts, and let the **Cantor–Bendixson rank** and **Cantor–Bendixson residue** refer to the usual transfinite derivative rank and its stable remainder. A shift has **maximality type infinity** if its maximality type is infinite; a shift of finite type is a shift defined by finitely many forbidden patterns, and a minimal subsystem is a subsystem minimal under inclusion.

**Cantor–Bendixson structure conjecture.** For all $d>1$, the Cantor–Bendixson rank of $\mathcal{S}^d$ is $\omega$. Furthermore, the Cantor–Bendixson residue is the closure of the set of shifts having maximality type infinity. The shifts which are not in this residue are precisely those that can be written as a finite union of shifts of finite type which are the limit of their minimal subsystems.

The preceding results show that shifts of maximality type infinity lie in the Cantor–Bendixson residue and that this set has empty interior, but they do not determine the full residue or the rank. The conjecture proposes a complete description of both the rank and the shifts outside the residue.

record.title: Papadimitriou–Yannakakis' completeness conjecture for minimum generating sets of quasigroups
record.statement:
A **quasigroup** is an algebra whose multiplication table is a Latin square; equivalently, for all elements $a,b$, there are unique elements $x,y$ such that $ax=b$ and $ya=b$. The **minimum generating set problem** asks whether a given quasigroup has a generating set of size at most $\log n$, where $n$ is the order of the quasigroup.

**Papadimitriou–Yannakakis' conjecture.** The minimum generating set problem for quasigroups is $\exists^{\log^2 n}\mathsf{P}$-complete.

Papadimitriou and Yannakakis established the analogous completeness result for arbitrary magmas and conjectured that completeness persists for the more structured class of quasigroups. The paper reports an unconditional refutation of a version of this conjecture for completeness under quasi-polynomial-size constant-depth reductions, and a refutation under polylogarithmic-space reductions assuming $\mathsf{EXP}\neq\mathsf{PSPACE}$, so the conjecture is treated as refuted.

record.title: Solovay-sequence conjecture on club HOD-Berkeley cardinals
record.statement:
Assume

$$
{\sf{AD}}_{\mathbb{R}}+V=L(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}))+“\Theta\text{ is a regular cardinal}”.
$$

Let $\Theta$ be the least ordinal not surjected by a real. Suppose $\zeta<\Theta$ is a successor member of the Solovay sequence, let $\nu$ be the largest member of the Solovay sequence below $\zeta$, set

$$
X=\bigcup_{\alpha<\zeta}\alpha^\omega,
$$

and let

$$
\Delta=\{A\subseteq\mathbb{R}:\text{the Wadge rank of }A\text{ is }<\nu\}.
$$

Assume also that $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})\cap{\sf{HOD}}_X=\Delta$. A cardinal $\kappa$ is a **club $N$-Berkeley cardinal** if for every $M\in N$ there is a club $C\subseteq\kappa$ such that for every $\alpha\in C$ there is an elementary embedding $j:M\to M$ with $\operatorname{crit}(j)=\alpha$.

**Solovay-sequence conjecture.** Under these assumptions, $V_\zeta^{{\sf{HOD}}_X}$ is a model of

$$
{\sf{ZF}+“\omega_1\text{ is a club }{\sf{HOD}}\text{-Berkeley cardinal}”.
$$

This predicts a specific inner model of determinacy and regular $\Theta$ has the stated Berkeley-cardinal property at $\omega_1$. No resolution is supplied in the source context.

record.title: Color class count function equivalence conjecture for partial colorings
record.statement:
Let $G_i'$ be the graph associated with a node $X_i$ of the smooth tree-decomposition, and let $f$ and $g$ be partial colorings of $G_i'$. For each tuple $\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}$ in $\mathcal{S}(X_i)$, let $CF_f\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\right)$ denote the number of color classes represented by the tuple, and let $CL_f\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\right)$ denote its color class function. **Color class count function equivalence conjecture.** If $f$ and $g$ have the same color class count function, namely

$$
CF_f\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\right)=CF_g\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\right)
$$

for every $\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\in\mathcal{S}(X_i)$, then there is a permutation $\pi$ of the colors such that

$$
CL_{\pi\circ f}\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\right)=CL_g\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j\le 9}\right)
$$

for every $\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\in\mathcal{S}(X_i)$. The conjecture would allow the algorithm to store color class count functions instead of full color class functions, potentially removing the restriction that the maximum degree $\Delta$ is constant and yielding a polynomial-time algorithm.

record.title: Weakened Minimal Resolution Conjecture for points in \(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^2\)
record.statement:
Let $N\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $U\subseteq(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^2)^N$ be a dense open subset. For $(P_1,P_2,\dots,P_N)\in U$, set $X=\{P_1,\dots,P_N\}$, and let $S/I_X$ be its coordinate ring with bigraded Betti numbers $\beta_{1,(i,j)}$. For a matrix $H$ indexed by $(i,j)\in\mathbb Z^2$, write

$$
DH=(\Delta^C)^2(\Delta^R)^3H.
$$

Let $H_X$ be the Hilbert matrix of $X$.

**Weakened Minimal Resolution Conjecture.** The set $X$ has a generic Hilbert matrix as in the source definition, and, for every fixed $(i,j)>(0,0)$, one has $\beta_{1,(i,j)}>0$ if and only if

$$
DH_X(i,j)<0\quad\text{and}\quad DH_X(i',j')\leq 0
$$

for all $(i',j')\leq(i,j)$ with $(i',j')\neq(0,0)$. Whenever this condition holds,

$$
\beta_{1,(i,j)}=-DH_X(i,j).
$$

This is a weakened version of the Minimal Resolution Conjecture for sufficiently general points in $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^2$: it only prescribes the first Betti numbers, but that control is intended to determine enough of the resolution to establish the paper's virtual-resolution results. The parser supplies no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved, so its status remains open.

record.title: Hong–Kang–Yu induced-cycle conjecture
record.statement:
Let $m$ and $l$ be positive integers. A graph is **$r$-connected** if it remains connected after deletion of any set of fewer than $r$ vertices. Let $G$ be a graph, let $e$ be an edge of $G$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_m$ be distinct vertices of $G-V(e)$. A cycle is **induced** if it has no chords in the graph containing it. **Hong–Kang–Yu's conjecture.** There exists a smallest positive integer $g(m,l)$ such that, for every $g(m,l)$-connected graph $G$, there is an induced cycle $C$ in $G-\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}$ containing $e$ and satisfying

$$
G-V(C)
$$

is $l$-connected. Hong, Kang, and Yu posed this as a strengthening of Lovász's conjecture, requiring the cycle to avoid prescribed vertices. The paper's results establish related cases for $l=2$ and $k=1,2$, but do not resolve this general induced-cycle assertion.

record.title: Uniqueness of the unitary group representation minimizer for HyperCube regularization
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a group operation table, and let $T$ be the tensor represented by the HyperCube factors. For a finite group, write $\varrho$ for its unitary regular representation, so that the factor slices satisfy

$$
A_g=B_g=C_g^\intercal=\varrho(g).
$$

Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote the HyperCube Regularizer and impose the constraint $T=D$.

**HyperCube regularizer minimizer conjecture.** The unitary group representation $A_g=B_g=C_g^\intercal=\varrho(g)$ describes the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{H}$ up to unitary basis changes, and its minimum regularizer loss is

$$
\mathcal{H}^*(D)=3\lVert D\rVert_F^2.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the regular representation is not only sufficient to reproduce every finite group operation table exactly, but is also the unique optimal solution, modulo unitary changes of basis, for the constrained HyperCube regularization problem.

record.title: The limiting row-membership probability conjecture for QUBO minimizers and maximizers
record.statement:
Let $\widetilde{J}=(J+J')/2$ be the symmetrized coupling matrix, let $\widetilde{H}$ be the Hamiltonian obtained by replacing $J$ with $\widetilde{J}$, and let $[i]$ denote the index of the $i$-th smallest row sum of $\widetilde{J}$. Thus $\eta^{\min}_{[i]}=1$ and $\eta^{\max}_{[i]}=1$ mean that the corresponding row belongs to the minimizer and maximizer, respectively.

**Limiting row-membership probability conjecture.** As $N\to\infty$,

$$
\mathbb{P}(\eta^{\min}_{[i]}=1)=f_{\min}\left(\frac{[i]}{N}\right)+o(1),
$$

where $f_{\min}$ is decreasing. Similarly,

$$
\mathbb{P}(\eta^{\max}_{[i]}=1)=f_{\max}\left(\frac{[i]}{N}\right)+o(1),
$$

with

$$
f_{\max}\left(\frac{[i]}{N}\right)=f_{\min}\left(1-\frac{[i]}{N}\right).
$$

Moreover, there exists $\lambda_0>0$ such that $f_{\min}(\lambda)=1$ for all $\lambda<\lambda_0$; if the tails of $J_{i,j}$ decay sufficiently fast, the limiting function does not depend on the distribution of $J_{i,j}$.

This conjecture proposes a universal, monotone limiting profile for membership in the minimizer and maximizer when rows are ordered by their row sums. The source gives numerical motivation but no proof or resolution; the maximizer probability line appears to contain a typographical omission in the supplied statement.

record.title: High-dimensional $p$ decoupling conjecture for smooth hypersurfaces
record.statement:
Let $\phi:\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\to\mathbb{R}$ be smooth, and let $\mathcal{M}_{\phi}=\{(\xi,\phi(\xi)):\xi\in[0,1]^{n-1}\}$. A set $S\subset[0,1]^{n-1}$ is $(\phi,\delta)$-flat when it satisfies the flatness condition defined in the paper. For a measurable function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ and measurable $S$, let $f_S$ denote the Fourier restriction of $f$ to $S\times\mathbb{R}$. **High-dimensional $p$ decoupling conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$, there is a sufficiently large $A=A(\epsilon)$ such that, for every $\delta>0$, one can find a finitely overlapping collection $\mathcal{S}_{\delta}$ of subsets of $[0,1]^{n-1}$ satisfying

$$
\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}_{\delta}}\chi_S\leq C_{\epsilon}\log(\delta^{-1}),
$$

with every $S$ $(\phi,A\delta)$-flat, and such that for $2\leq p\leq\frac{2(n+1)}{n-1}$,

$$
\|f\|_{L^p}\leq C_{\epsilon}\delta^{-\epsilon}(\#\mathcal{S}_{\delta})^{\frac12-\frac1p}\left(\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}_{\delta}}\|f_S\|_{L^p}^p\right)^{\frac1p}
$$

for all $f$ whose Fourier supports are contained in $N_{\delta}(\mathcal{M}_{\phi})$. This is proposed as a possible extension of $\ell^p$ decoupling to higher dimensions; the statement is conjectural for general smooth $\phi$.

record.title: Low-complexity encoding conjecture for hypergraph Ramsey colorings
record.statement:
A **pair construction** of a $3$-graph coloring is a coloring of $K_N^{(3)}$ obtained from functions $f:\binom{[N]}{2}\to[p]$ and $g:[p]^3\to\{\operatorname{red},\operatorname{blue}\}$ by setting

$$
\chi_{f,g}(\{i,j,k\})=g(f(i,j),f(j,k),f(k,i))
$$

for $i<j<k$. Its complexity is $p$. For $3$-graphs $G,H$, let $r^p(G,H)$ be the smallest $n$ such that every $2$-edge-coloring of $K_n^{(3)}$ of complexity at most $p$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$. **Low-complexity encoding conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $a>0$ such that, for all $3$-graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$
r^p(G,H)\ge r(G,H)^a
$$

whenever $p>r(G,H)^{o(1)}$. This conjecture asks whether Ramsey colorings can retain a polynomial fraction of the unrestricted Ramsey number while using subpolynomial pair-construction complexity. The source gives no resolution.

record.title: The Lefschetz and Hodge–Riemann strengthening of Almkvist's conjecture
record.statement:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers and define the graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra

$$
A(m,n)=\frac{{\mathbb Q}[e_1,\ldots,e_n]}{(e_1(m),\ldots,e_n(m))}.
$$

If $A(m,n)$ has socle degree $d$, its strong Lefschetz property (SLP) means that there is a linear form $\ell\in A_1$ for which

$$
\times\ell^{d-2i}\colon A_i\longrightarrow A_{d-i},\qquad 0\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac d2\right\rfloor,
$$

are all isomorphisms. The Lefschetz property with respect to the Hilbert function (HLP) means that these maps have rank equal to the minimum dimension of the graded components between $i$ and $d-i$. The complex Hodge–Riemann relations (complex HRR) mean that these maps have signature equal to the alternating sum of the even first differences of the Hilbert function.

**Almkvist–Lefschetz strengthening.** (i) For each $m$, the algebra $A(m,n)$ satisfies the SLP for all $n\geq 11$. (ii) Moreover, if $m$ is even, then $A(m,n)$ satisfies the SLP for all $n$. (iii) For each $m$, the algebra $A(m,n)$ satisfies HLP for all $n$. (iv) If $m$ is even, then $A(m,n)$ satisfies the complex HRR.

SLP implies unimodality of the Hilbert function, so the first two assertions strengthen Almkvist's conjecture; the latter assertions concern finer Lefschetz and signature properties. The source states that items (i)–(iii) were posed in earlier work and item (iv) is new, but gives no resolution of these assertions.

record.title: The uniform-distribution conjecture for temporal-clique label intervals
record.statement:
Let $G_{n,\delta}$ be an Erdős–Rényi random graph, and construct a temporal instance ${\cal I}(G_{n,\delta})$ by assigning labels to the edges of $G_{n,\delta}$ independently and uniformly at random in $[0,\delta]$, and assigning labels to all other edges independently and uniformly at random in $[\delta,1]$. For a vertex set $Q$, define its label interval by

$$
\Delta(Q)=\left[\min(\lambda(e):e\in Q),\max(\lambda(e):e\in Q)\right].
$$

Let $Q^*$ be the $\delta$-clique constructed by algorithm ${\cal A}_{SRT}$ on instance ${\cal I}(G_{n,\delta})$. **Uniform-distribution conjecture.** Then $\Delta(Q^*)$ is distributed almost uniformly at random within $[0,1]$. This conjecture concerns the distribution of the interval containing the labels of an algorithmically found temporal clique and is proposed as a possible route toward proving the reduction from temporal-clique approximation to maximum-clique approximation in Erdős–Rényi graphs; no proof or resolution is given.

record.title: The Naisargik mapping between quaternary and binary Helberg codes
record.statement:
Let $H(n,q,s,a)$ denote a Helberg code with length $n$, alphabet size $q$, deletion parameter $s$, and residue $a$. Let $a$ be the residue corresponding to the maximum number of codewords in $H(n,4,1,a)$, and let $a'$ be the corresponding binary-code residue. **Naisargik mapping conjecture.** There is a one-to-one mapping $\phi$ between the codewords of $H(n,4,1,a)$ and $H(2n,2,2,a')$ such that, for every codeword $c\in H(n,4,1,a)$, $\phi(c)\in H(2n,2,2,a')$, and

$$
\phi(H(n,4,1,a))=H(2n,2,2,a').
$$

Thus all codewords of the Naisargik image satisfy $\phi(H(n,4,1,a))\subseteq H(2n,2,2,a')$. The mapping is used in the paper's argument relating deletion correction in quaternary Helberg codes to correction in their binary Naisargik images; the supplied text gives no independent resolution evidence for this assertion.

record.title: The amazing-hypercube $R$-element conjecture
record.statement:
Let $W$ be a Coxeter group of type $A$, and let $u,v\in W$ with $u\leq v$. An upper hypercube decomposition $z\in [u,v]$ is called **amazing** when, for every $x\in [u,v]$, the intersection $[z,v]\cap[x,v]$ has a minimum $z\vee x$, and this minimum is a hypercube decomposition of $[x,v]$. Write $W^z_{[u,v]}$ for the associated set of elements used in the $R$-element expansion, and let $\widetilde{R}_{u,v}$ denote the Kazhdan–Lusztig $\widetilde{R}$-polynomial.

**Amazing-hypercube $R$-element conjecture.** The element $z$ is an $R$-element, meaning that

$$
\widetilde{R}_{u,v}=\sum_{p\in W^z_{[u,v]}}q^{\operatorname{d}(u,p)}\widetilde{R}_{p,v}.
$$

This is presented as a weak version of a conjecture from Brenti and Marietti, which had been verified up to $W=S_6$. The assertion is intended to provide a combinatorial route toward the Kazhdan–Lusztig combinatorial invariance conjecture.

record.title: Khot's unique games conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, and consider an instance of the two-variable linear system $2$-Lin-$k$ over $\mathbb{Z}_k$, with equations

$$
\mathbf{x}_i=\mathbf{x}_j+\mathbf{b}_l\pmod{k}.
$$

An assignment is a map $\mathbf{x}=\{\mathbf{x}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{x}_n\}$ with each variable taking a value in $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$. **Unique games conjecture.** For every $0<\epsilon<\frac{1}{2}$, given an instance in which a $1-\epsilon$ fraction of equations can be satisfied, there exists a value of $k$ such that no polynomial-time algorithm can find a solution satisfying at least an $\epsilon$ fraction of the equations. This is a central hardness assumption in approximation complexity and underlies optimality results for problems such as MAX-CUT. The source does not provide evidence resolving the conjecture.

record.title: Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture on zeta maxima over mesoscopic intervals
record.statement:
Let $\theta\in(-1,0]$, let $T$ tend to infinity, and let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$. Write $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ for a standard Gaussian random variable, and let $\mathcal{M}$ be a random variable that is $O(1)$ in probability, independent of $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, with a tail of the form $Cye^{-2y}$. **Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture.** The maximum satisfies

$$
\max_{h\leq\log^\theta T}\log\left|\zeta\left(\tfrac{1}{2}+i\tau+ih\right)\right|\sim(1+\theta)\log\log T-\frac{3}{4}\log\log\log T+\sqrt{\tfrac{|\theta|}{2}\log\log T}\,\mathcal{N}(0,1)+\mathcal{M}.
$$

This conjecture describes the extreme values of the Riemann zeta function on mesoscopic intervals, incorporating both Gaussian fluctuations and an order-one extremal correction. The cited formulation is presented as a prediction from connections with log-correlated processes; its resolution is not supplied here.

record.title: Even-dimensional monomial distance conjecture over finite p-adic rings
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a sufficiently large prime, let $r$ be a positive integer, and let $E_1,E_2$ be subsets of $(\mathbb{Z}/p^r\mathbb{Z})^n$. For a polynomial

$$
F(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i^k
$$

with even $n\geq 2$, $k\geq 2$, and $a_i\neq 0$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$, define

$$
\Delta_{n,r}(E_1,E_2)=\{F(\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}):\mathbf{x}\in E_1,\ \mathbf{y}\in E_2\}
$$

and

$$
\delta_{E_1,E_2}=\frac{\sqrt{|E_1||E_2|}}{p^{rn}}.
$$

**Even-dimensional monomial distance conjecture.** If $\delta_{E_1,E_2}\gg p^{-n/2}$, then

$$
|\Delta_{n,r}(E_1,E_2)|\gg p^r.
$$

The conjecture proposes an $r$-uniform density threshold for even-dimensional diagonal monomial distance problems over finite $p$-adic rings. The preceding theorem establishes a related bound for general diagonal polynomials, but its density threshold is independent of $r$ only when the minimum exponent is $2$; the proposed statement remains unproved in the source.

record.title: The conjecture that random generalized power series are irreducible
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and let $b\in K((\mathbb{R}^{\leq 0}))$ be a random generalized power series, meaning that either $\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{supp}(b))-\{0\}$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-linearly independent or the tuple of coefficients indexed by $\operatorname{supp}(b)$ is algebraically independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. Let $\sup(b)$ be the supremum of the support, $\operatorname{ot}(b)$ its order type, and define $\deg(b)$ as the maximum ordinal $\alpha$ such that $\omega^\alpha\leq\operatorname{ot}(b)$. **Random-series irreducibility conjecture.** If $\sup(b)=0$, then $b$ is irreducible, and so is $b+r$ for every series $r$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{ot}(r)<\omega^{\deg(b)}.
$$

The paper proves this assertion for substantial families of order types and notes that the conjecture would extend those results to all random series; its general status is not specified.

record.title: Fu–Tang's parity-separated partition inequality
record.statement:
Let $\overline{\mathcal P}_{\operatorname{eu}}^{\operatorname{ou}}(n)$ be the set of partitions described in the source in which the largest even part has odd multiplicity and every other part has even multiplicity, and let $\overline p_{\operatorname{eu}}^{\operatorname{ou}}(n)$ denote its cardinality. $$
\overline p_{\operatorname{eu}}^{\operatorname{ou}}(2n)<\overline p^{\operatorname{eu}}_{\operatorname{ou}}(2n+1).
$$
 The conjecture compares the two partition-counting sequences associated with parity-separated partitions and additional multiplicity conditions. The source attributes it to Fu and Tang; no resolution is given here.

record.title: The subhypercube construction conjecture for higher-dimensional queens
record.statement:
Let $d$ be an integer, let $m$ be given, and let $n>m$ with $n=m+k$. A **regular solution** to the $(n,d)$-queens problem is a solution containing a subset of size $k^d$ with $p$ queens. The $(m,d)$-board is the board of side length $m$ in dimension $d$.

**Subhypercube construction conjecture.** For all $d$ and such $m,n,k$, if there exists a regular solution to the $(n,d)$-queens problem containing a subset of size $k^d$ with $p$ queens, then one can construct a partial solution of

$$
n^{d-1}-dkn^{d-2}+\frac{(d-1)(d-2)}{2}k^2n^{d-3}+\dots+(-1)^{d-1}a\cdot p
$$

queens on the $(m,d)$-board. The last-term integer $a$ is negative for even $d$ and positive for odd $d$.

This generalizes the explicitly constructed three- and four-dimensional cases. It is intended to describe how a solution on a larger board yields a partial solution after cutting off layers, but the general construction remains to be shown.

record.title: Asymptotic uncovered-vertex probability for dense almost-regular hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ be a positive integer and let $0<\delta,\varepsilon<1$ be positive real numbers. There is an $n_0$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$, if $H$ is an $n$-vertex $k$-graph whose vertex degrees lie between $(1-n^{-\delta})d$ and $(1+n^{-\delta})d$ for some $d>n^{\varepsilon}$, and whose maximum codegree is at most $n^{-\delta}d$, then, for a uniformly random matching $M$ of $H$, writing $\mathcal{P}_H(\overline{v})$ for the probability that $M$ does not cover $v$, **the dense almost-regularity conjecture.** For every $v\in V(H)$,

$$
\mathcal{P}_H(\overline{v})=(1+o_n(1))d^{-1/k}.
$$

This is posed in the concluding remarks as the regime in which the disproved regular-linear conjecture may still hold: the paper's counterexamples rely on fixed $d$ and very large constructions, while the claim concerns degrees growing faster than a power of $n$.

record.title: Generic double multiplicity conjecture for symmetric singular matrix pencils
record.statement:
Let $A-\lambda B$ be a real symmetric singular $n\times n$ pencil with normal rank $n-k$, and let $D_A-\lambda D_B$ be a real symmetric regular $k\times k$ pencil. For a matrix $U\in\mathbb R^{n,k}$ and a nonzero scalar $\tau\in\mathbb R$, consider the rank-$k$ perturbation

$$
A-\lambda B+\tau U(D_A-\lambda D_B)U^\top.
$$

**Generic double multiplicity conjecture.** There exists a generic set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{n,k}$ such that, for every $U\in\Omega$ and every $\tau\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, the spectrum of the perturbed pencil consists of the eigenvalues of $A-\lambda B$ (true eigenvalues), the eigenvalues of $D_A-\lambda D_B$ (prescribed eigenvalues), and random eigenvalues, all of which have algebraic multiplicity precisely two. This conjecture extends the rank-one result for pencils with one minimal index; the observed real-symmetric examples exhibit random eigenvalues in double pairs.

record.title: The half-order conjecture for locating-dominating sets in twin-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph. A set $C\subseteq V(G)$ is a **locating-dominating set** if it dominates every vertex outside $C$ and, for every two distinct vertices $u,v\in V(G)\setminus C$, the sets $N(u)\cap C$ and $N(v)\cap C$ are distinct. Write $\gamma^{LD}(G)$ for the minimum cardinality of a locating-dominating set, and let $n=|V(G)|$ be the order of $G$. A graph is **twin-free** if it has neither two vertices with equal open neighborhoods nor two vertices with equal closed neighborhoods; an isolated vertex has degree zero. **The half-order conjecture.** Every twin-free graph $G$ of order $n$ without isolated vertices satisfies

$$
\gamma^{LD}(G)\leq \frac{n}{2}.
$$

This conjecture, originally proposed in the cited work and subsequently studied in the cited formulation, asserts a sharp universal upper bound for locating-dominating sets in twin-free graphs. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied source material.

record.title: Folklore coupling-independence conjecture for proper list-colorings
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $(L_v)_{v\in V}$ be color lists. A proper list-coloring assigns to each vertex $v$ a color in $L_v$ so that adjacent vertices receive different colors. The associated uniform distribution is called **$O_\delta(1)$-coupling independent** when its coupling-independence parameter is bounded by a constant depending only on $\delta$.

**Folklore conjecture.** Let $\delta>0$ be a constant. If

$$
\left\vert L_v\right\vert\geq (1+\delta)\Delta+O(1)
$$

for every $v\in V$, then the uniform distribution $\mu$ over all proper list-colorings of $G$ is $O_\delta(1)$-coupling independent.

This conjecture would establish coupling independence at essentially the $(1+\delta)\Delta$ list-size threshold for arbitrary, possibly unbounded-degree graphs, and would remove the stronger color-list requirement used by the paper's main rapid-mixing result. The source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

record.title: Layered 3-graph characterization of vanishing codegree Turán density
record.statement:
A $3$-graph $F$ is **layered** if there is a function $f:V(F)\to\mathbb N$ such that: every edge has exactly one vertex whose label is strictly greater than the other two; edges with the same maximum label have the same multiset of labels; and whenever edges $uvw$ and $u'v'w'$ satisfy $f(u)=f(u')$ and $f(v)=f(v')$, they also satisfy $f(w)=f(w')$. Let $\pi_{\mathrm{co}}(F)$ denote the codegree Turán density of $F$, and let $\pi_{\mathrm{u}}(F)$ denote its uniform Turán density. **Layered 3-graph conjecture.** For every $3$-graph $F$,

$$
\pi_{\mathrm{co}}(F)=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F\text{ is layered and }\pi_{\mathrm{u}}(F)=0.
$$

The paper proves this equivalence for layered $3$-graphs, so the conjecture asserts that the layered condition is also necessary. The supplied text gives no resolution of the full characterization.

record.title: Converse-invariant orientations of trees with maximum degree at least three
record.statement:
Let $D$ be an orientation of a tree with maximum degree at least $3$. Write $-D$ for the converse orientation, and say that $D$ is **converse invariant** when it has the same number of copies in every tournament as $-D$. The **bridge-mirroring operation** is the operation defined in the paper that mirrors an oriented bridge; recursively applying it produces orientations from an orientation of a path.

**Conjecture on converse-invariant tree orientations.** $D$ is converse invariant if and only if

$$
D\cong -D
$$

or $D$ can be obtained by applying the bridge-mirroring operation recursively to an orientation of a path.

The paper establishes this characterization for orientations of trees with diameter bounded by three. The conjecture proposes that the same description holds for all orientations of trees with maximum degree at least $3$.

record.title: Cyclotomic-class partition conjecture for products of primes congruent to $1$ modulo $6$
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a product of primes, each of which has the form $6k+1$. For $t>1$, let $\operatorname{Cos}(t)$ be the union of all binary $2$-cyclotomic classes of size $t$, and let $N_t$ be the number of those classes. For $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}_{2^n-1}\setminus\{0\}$, write $\operatorname{Cyc}\Gamma(a)$ for the union of the cyclotomic classes indexed by the elements of $\Gamma(a)$.

**Cyclotomic partition conjecture.** For every integer $t>1$, there are $N_t/18$ pairs $(a_i,b_i)$, $i=1,\ldots,N_t/18$, such that

$$
\operatorname{Cos}(t)=\dot\bigcup_i\bigl(\operatorname{Cyc}\Gamma(a_i)\,\dot\cup\,\operatorname{Cyc}\Gamma(b_i)\,\dot\cup\,\operatorname{Cyc}\Gamma(a_i+b_i)\bigr).
$$

Such a partition would group the relevant binary cyclotomic classes into triples of six-class configurations and is used to construct symmetric balanced triangle designs. The supplied text gives the assertion as a proposition-like statement but provides no resolution evidence.

record.title: Minimality conjecture for the BPD energy in the plane
record.statement:
Let $N\in\mathbb N\backslash\{0,1\}$ and let $X_N\in(\mathbb R^2)^N$ be a configuration of $N$ points. For the potential $V_{\textnormal{BPD}}$ and its energy $\textnormal{E}_{\textnormal{BPD}}$, let $Z_N$ denote the specified square-lattice configuration and let $\mathcal{E}_{\|\cdot\|_\infty}(N)$ be the minimum energy for the corresponding norm energy on $\mathbb Z^2$.

**Minimality for $\textnormal{E}_{\textnormal{BPD}}$ in general.** For all $N\in\mathbb N\backslash\{0,1\}$, we have

$$
\min_{X_N\in(\mathbb R^2)^N}\textnormal{E}_{\textnormal{BPD}}(X_N)=\mathcal{E}_{\|\cdot\|_\infty}(N)=-\lfloor4N-\sqrt{28N-12}\rfloor,
$$

achieved in particular for $X_N=Z_N$.

This conjecture asserts crystallization of finite minimizers for the BPD potential: the minimum over arbitrary planar configurations equals the square-lattice minimum, with a square-lattice minimizer. The corresponding minimality result is known when configurations are constrained to $\mathbb Z^2$, while the unrestricted finite-$N$ crystallization statement remains open.

record.title: The colour-bias threshold conjecture for tight Hamilton cycles in 2-coloured 4-graphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a $2$-edge-coloured $4$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices, and let $\delta_1(H)$ denote its minimum vertex degree. A tight Hamilton cycle is a cyclic ordering of all vertices such that every four consecutive vertices form an edge; its colour-bias is the excess of the number of edges in one colour over the number in the other. **The colour-bias tight Hamilton-cycle conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, there are $\gamma>0$ and $n_0\in\mathbb N$ such that every $2$-edge-coloured $4$-graph $H$ on $n\geq n_0$ vertices with

$$
\delta_1(H)\geq\left(\frac{365}{512}+\varepsilon\right)\binom{n}{3}
$$

contains a tight Hamilton cycle with colour-bias above $\gamma n$. The conjectured threshold is motivated by a construction partitioning the vertices into parts of sizes $7n/8$ and $n/8$, showing that a higher threshold than the one for colour-bias perfect matchings is necessary in the $4$-uniform case.

record.title: Two-axis extremizer conjecture for the radius-$\sqrt{2}$ reverse Littlewood–Offord problem
record.statement:
For each sufficiently large integer $n$, let $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ be arbitrary unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$, and let $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n$ be independent Rademacher random variables. For an integer $t$ with $t\leq n$, define $v_i'=(1,0)$ for $i\leq t$ and $v_i'=(0,1)$ for $i>t$. **Two-axis extremizer conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$, there exists some $t\leq n$ such that

$$
\mathbb{P}[\\|\epsilon_1v_1+\cdots+\epsilon_nv_n\\|_2\leq\sqrt{2}]\geq\mathbb{P}[\\|\epsilon_1v_1'+\cdots+\epsilon_nv_n'\\|_2\leq\sqrt{2}].
$$

This asks whether the smallest radius-$\sqrt{2}$ concentration probability is attained by a configuration consisting of copies of the two coordinate-axis vectors. The source presents it as an open stronger statement and notes that it would identify the relevant extremal configuration.

record.title: The global extreme-zero product conjecture for transitional Laguerre polynomials
record.statement:
For $n=0,1,\dots$ and $\alpha>-1$, define the transitional Laguerre polynomials $\widehat{L}^{(\alpha)}_{n+1}(\cdot,t)$ by

$$
\widehat{L}^{(\alpha)}_{n+1}(\cdot,t)=(x-(2n+\alpha+1))L^{(\alpha)}_n(x)-n(n+\alpha)t^2L^{(\alpha)}_{n-1}(x),
$$

where

$$
L^{(\alpha)}_{-1}=0,\qquad \widehat{L}^{(\alpha)}_n=(-1)^n n!L^{(\alpha)}_n.
$$

Let the extreme zeros denote the smallest and largest zeros of a polynomial. **Global extreme-zero product conjecture.** For all $\alpha>-1$, $n=5,6,\dots$, and $t\in(0,1]$, the product of the extreme zeros of $\widehat{L}^{(\alpha)}_{n+1}(\cdot,t)$ is greater than the product of the extreme zeros of $\widehat{L}^{(\alpha)}_{n+1}(\cdot,0)$.

This extends the proposition's partial result, which covers only $-1<\alpha\leq47.9603$ and $t\in[0,0.568774]$. Numerical evidence includes the Hermite-related cases $\alpha=\pm1/2$ and $t=1$, but the assertion for all admissible $\alpha$, all $n\geq5$, and $t\in(0,1]$ remains open.

record.title: Conjecture on arbitrarily oscillating win-probability derivatives
record.statement:
Let ${\normalfont{\operatorname{Win}}}(v,w;p)$ denote the probability that the binary word $v$ occurs before the binary word $w$ in an iid Bernoulli$(p)$ sequence.

**Oscillation conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, for every positive integer $k$, there is a pair of binary words $(v,w)$ with lengths at most $\exp(Ck)$ for which

$$
\frac{d}{dp}{\normalfont{\operatorname{Win}}}(v,w;p)
$$

changes sign at least $k$ times as $p$ ranges over $(0,1)$.

Win probabilities are rational functions of $p$, with endpoint values constrained to $\{0,\frac12,1\}$. The conjecture predicts that despite this algebraic structure, derivatives of win-probability functions can exhibit arbitrarily many sign changes using pairs whose word lengths grow only exponentially in the number of changes. The source presents this as supported by heuristic arguments and computer checks, with no resolution given.

record.title: Piecewise planar spectral-extremal graph conjecture for fixed edge count
record.statement:
Let $G_m$ denote the graph defined earlier in the paper as the large-edge spectral-extremal planar graph, and let $H_m$ be defined by

$$
H_m=\begin{cases}
K_2\vee P_{\frac{m}{3}},&\text{if }m\bmod 3=0,\\
K_1\vee\left((K_1\vee P_{\frac{m-1}{3}})\cup K_1\right),&\text{if }m\bmod 3=1,\\
K_2\vee\left(P_{\frac{m-2}{3}}\cup K_1\right),&\text{if }m\bmod 3=2.
\end{cases}
$$

Here $\cup$ denotes disjoint union and $\vee$ denotes join. **Fixed-edge-count planar spectral-extremal conjecture.** The planar graph with $m$ edges and maximum spectral radius is

$$
\begin{cases}
G_m,&\text{for }m\geq 33\text{ or }m=31,\\
H_m,&\text{for }m\leq 30\text{ or }m=32.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture aims to complete the paper's determination of spectral-extremal planar graphs beyond the sufficiently-large-edge regime, but the excerpt gives no resolution.

record.title: Conjecture on irreducible components of varieties with symmetric compound matrices
record.statement:
Let $N$ be the matrix-size parameter, let $[N+1]=\{1,\ldots,N+1\}$, and let $S=S^2\mathbb{C}^{N+1}$ be the subspace of symmetric $(N+1)\times(N+1)$ matrices. For $r\in[N+1]$, define

$$
\mathcal{SC}_r=\{B\in\mathbb{C}^{(N+1)\times(N+1)}\mid C_r(B)\text{ is symmetric}\},
$$

where $C_r(B)$ is the $r$th compound matrix of $B$, and write $(X_j)_{S_j}^\vee$ for the relative dual variety introduced earlier. Let $A=\bigwedge^2\mathbb{C}^{N+1}$ denote the space of skew-symmetric matrices. **Irreducible-component conjecture.** For every $r\in[N+1]$: (i) $\mathcal{SC}_1=S=S^2\mathbb{C}^{N+1}$ is an irreducible component of $\mathcal{SC}_r$; (ii) $(X_{n-r})_{S_{n-r}}^\vee$ is an irreducible component of $\mathcal{SC}_r$ for every $2\le r\le N+1$; and (iii) $A=\bigwedge^2\mathbb{C}^{N+1}$ is an irreducible component of $\mathcal{SC}_r$ for all $N\ge 3$ and even $r\in[N]$. The conjecture is motivated by symbolic computations for $N=2$ and $N=3$, which exhibit several of these components, while the preceding example also shows that the varieties $\mathcal{SC}_i$ need not be nested. Determining all irreducible components in general remains open.

record.title: Exact bipartite Komlós–Sárközy–Szemerédi conjecture
record.statement:
A bipartite graph $G=(A,B,E)$ is **balanced** when its two parts have equal size, and $\delta(G)$ denotes its minimum degree. A **balanced rooted tree** on $2n$ vertices has $n$ vertices in each partition class, and $\Delta(T)$ denotes its maximum degree.

**Exact bipartite Komlós–Sárközy–Szemerédi conjecture.** For each $\gamma>0$, there are $c,n_0>0$ such that for every $n\ge n_0$, if $G=(A,B,E)$ is a balanced bipartite graph on $2n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge(\frac12+\gamma)n$, and $T$ is a balanced rooted tree on $2n$ vertices with $\Delta(T)\le\frac{cn}{\log n}$, then $T$ embeds in $G$ with the root of $T$ embedded in $A$.

This is proposed as the direct bipartite analogue of the Komlós–Sárközy–Szemerédi theorem. The source describes it as a belief rather than a proved result, so it remains open.

record.title: Haar-wavelet solvability conjecture for near-Tsirelson Bell-CHSH violations
record.statement:
Fix $\eta\in(\sqrt2-1,1)$. Let $N_0<N_1$ and $K>1$ determine a finite Haar-wavelet resolution, and define $\widetilde f,\widetilde f',\widetilde g,\widetilde g'$ by finite linear combinations of the Haar wavelets as in the paper. The coefficients are required to satisfy the normalization and inner-product equations

$$
\begin{array}{l}
\langle\widetilde f\mid\widetilde f\rangle=\langle\widetilde f'\mid\widetilde f'\rangle=\langle\widetilde g\mid\widetilde g\rangle=\langle\widetilde g'\mid\widetilde g'\rangle=1,\\
\langle\widetilde f\mid\widetilde g\rangle=\langle\widetilde f'\mid\widetilde g\rangle=\langle\widetilde f\mid\widetilde g'\rangle=-\langle\widetilde f'\mid\widetilde g'\rangle=-i\frac{\sqrt2\eta}{1+\eta^2}.
\end{array}
$$

**Haar-wavelet solvability conjecture.** For every $\eta\in(\sqrt2-1,1)$, a resolution $\{N_0,N_1,K\}$ can be found such that this finite system admits a solution of the prescribed Haar-wavelet expansion form.

If true, the conjecture would provide an exact finite-resolution construction of Bell-CHSH violations approaching Tsirelson's bound in the vacuum state of the free massless $(1+1)$-dimensional spinor field. The paper presents evidence for the claim, while no proof or disproof is supplied.

record.title: Degree and nilpotence-index conjectures for the modified Hecke operator at 19 modulo 5
record.statement:
Let $p=5$, let $k\geq 1$ with $5\nmid k$, and let $D_{19}(k,5)$ denote the degree in $\Delta$ of $\Delta^k\mid T_{19}^{\prime}$ modulo $5$. Define $v_5(n)$ to be the largest power of $5$ dividing $n$, and let $S_{19}^{\prime}(k,5)$ be the least $t\geq 1$ for which the $t$th iterate of the degree-lowering function reaches $-\infty$. If $k=\sum a_i5^i$ and $s=a_0+5a_1$, define $c_t=S_{19}^{\prime}(5^t+1,5)-1$.

**Degree and nilpotence-index conjecture.** The degree $D_{19}(k,5)$ is given by the displayed residue-class formulas in the source; moreover, $c_0=0$, $c_1=2$, and

$$
c_i=3c_{i-1}+2c_{i-2}\quad(i\geq2),
$$

and

$$
S_{19}^{\prime}(k,5)=S_{19}^{\prime}(s,5)+\sum_{i\geq2}a_ic_i.
$$

Further,

$$
S_{19}^{\prime}(k,5)=O(k^{\alpha}),\qquad \alpha=\log_5\left(\frac{3+\sqrt{17}}2\right)\approx0.7892,
$$

and $N_{19}(\Delta^k,5)\leq S_{19}^{\prime}(k,5)$.

record.title: List-coloring transfer meta-conjecture for graph classes
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a natural graph class, and let $k$ be a positive integer. For a graph $G$ with a $k$-assignment $L$, let $\mathcal{C}_L(G)$ be the graph of proper $L$-colorings, with edges joining colorings that differ at one vertex. **List-coloring transfer meta-conjecture.** If there is a constant $C_{k,\mathcal{G}}$ such that $\operatorname{diam}\mathcal{C}_{[k]}(G)\le C_{k,\mathcal{G}}|G|$ for every $G\in\mathcal{G}$ with the uniform assignment $[k]=\\{1,\ldots,k\\}$, then there is a constant $C'_{k,\mathcal{G}}$ such that $\operatorname{diam}\mathcal{C}_L(G)\le C'_{k,\mathcal{G}}|G|$ for every $G\in\mathcal{G}$ and every $k$-assignment $L$. The paper specifically proposes this for classes of bounded maximum average degree and for planar graphs of prescribed girth; it remains open in this generality.

record.title: The $l^p$ restriction conjecture for uniformly bounded orthonormal systems
record.statement:
Let $2\le q<p<\infty$, and let $\Phi$ be a finite, uniformly bounded orthonormal system. For a finite collection $\Theta$ of functions, define $K_p^*(\Theta)$ to be the smallest constant such that

$$
\left\|\sum_{n=1}^{N}a_n\varphi_n\right\|_p\le K_p^*(\Theta)N^{\frac12-\frac1p}\left(\sum_{n=1}^{N}|a_n|^p\right)^{1/p}
$$

for every choice of coefficients, where $\Theta=\{\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_N\}$. **The $l^p$ restriction conjecture.** There exists a subset $\Psi\subset\Phi$ satisfying

$$
K_p^*(\Psi)\lesssim 1\quad\text{and}\quad |\Psi|\sim K_q^*(\Phi)^{-2q/p}|\Phi|^{q/p}.
$$

This conjecture is an $l^p$ analogue of the corresponding selection result for $K_p$ constants. It would provide large subsets with uniformly bounded $K_p^*$ constant in terms of the $K_q^*$ behaviour of the original orthonormal system; the statement is presented as a conjecture because the proof of the analogous theorem has critical steps that do not directly translate to the $l^p$ setting.

record.title: One-cluster convergence conjecture for causal attention with a multidimensional dominant eigenspace
record.statement:
Let $Q$ and $K$ be arbitrary matrices, and let $V$ be a matrix whose largest eigenvalue $\lambda_{\max}>0$ is real, with eigenspace $L$ satisfying $\mathop{\rm dim} L\geq2$. Assume that $Vz\in L^{\perp}$ and $\langle Vz,z\rangle<\lambda_{\max}|z|^2$ for every $z\in L^{\perp}$. For an initialization $(x_1(0),\ldots,x_n(0))$, let $\mathbf{P}_{L^{\perp}}$ denote orthogonal projection onto $L^{\perp}$, set $y_1:=\mathbf{P}_{L^{\perp}}(x_1(0))$, and define $\xi:=y_1/|y_1|$. **One-cluster convergence conjecture.** For almost every initialization, the causal attention dynamics converge to one cluster, specifically

$$
\forall k\in[n],\qquad \lim_{t\to\infty}x_k(t)=\xi.
$$

This is the proposed description of the positive-dominant-eigenvalue case when the dominant eigenspace has dimension at least two. The paper presents it as a conjectural generalization because critical manifolds make the corresponding stable-manifold analysis technically difficult; no resolution is given.

record.title: The iterated-tripartite classification conjecture for off-diagonal 3-graph Ramsey numbers
record.statement:
A **3-graph** is a 3-uniform hypergraph, and $r(H,K_n^{(3)})$ denotes the smallest $N$ such that every red/blue-coloring of the edges of the complete 3-graph $K_N^{(3)}$ contains either a red copy of $H$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(3)}$. An **iterated blowup of an edge** is a complete tripartite 3-graph, or a 3-graph formed by repeatedly placing another iterated blowup in one or more parts; a 3-graph is **iterated tripartite** when it is contained in such a blowup.

**The iterated-tripartite classification conjecture.** For a 3-graph $H$, there exists a constant $c$ depending only on $H$ such that

$$
r(H,K_n^{(3)})\leq n^c
$$

for all $n$ if and only if $H$ is a subgraph of an iterated blowup of an edge.

The forward direction would classify exactly which 3-graphs have polynomial off-diagonal Ramsey numbers. The polynomial upper bound for iterated tripartite 3-graphs was already known, while the converse remains open.

record.title: Kahn–Kalai threshold conjecture for graph appearances
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and write $v(G)$ and $e(G)$ for its numbers of vertices and edges. For a subgraph $F\subseteq G$, define $p_E(G)$ to be the smallest $p$ such that

$$
\frac{v(F)!}{|\operatorname{Aut}(F)|}p^{e(F)}\geq 1
$$

for every $F\subseteq G$. A **threshold function** for a sequence of graphs $\{G_n\}$ is a function ${\rm th}(G_n)$ such that, for the random graph $G(n,p(n))$, the appearance probability tends to one when $p(n)/{\rm th}(G_n)\to\infty$ and tends to zero when $p(n)/{\rm th}(G_n)\to 0$. **Kahn–Kalai threshold conjecture.** There is a universal constant $K$ such that, for every sequence $\{G_n\}$, a threshold function for the appearance of $\{G_n\}$ in $G(n,p)$ is at most

$$
p_E(G_n)\log |v(G_n)|.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the first-moment obstruction determines thresholds up to a logarithmic factor, uniformly over all graph sequences. It was proposed by Kahn and Kalai; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

record.title: The forbidden-pattern characterization conjecture for one-stack one-queue layouts
record.statement:
Let an ordered matching have a fixed non-separated layout. A **$1$-stack $1$-queue layout** uses one stack and one queue, and a **mixed layout on $1$ page** uses one page whose edges may be assigned to stacks or queues. The twelve and eight patterns referred to below are the patterns depicted in the source's figures.

**Forbidden-pattern characterization conjecture.** The ordered matching admits

$$
\text{a $1$-stack $1$-queue layout if and only if it avoids the 12 patterns depicted in the source's figure,}
$$

and admits a mixed layout on one page if and only if it avoids the 8 patterns depicted in the source's figure.

This conjecture proposes complete finite obstruction sets for the two smallest non-separated layout classes. It is consistent with the preceding computational enumeration of twelve and eight critical matchings, but the supplied source gives no proof or resolution.

record.title: Mazur–Tate's multiplicative refined BSD conjecture
record.statement:
Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ have split multiplicative reduction at a prime $p$, put $G_p=\left(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\right)^*/\langle-1\rangle$, and let $\lambda(a,p)$ be the even modular symbol. Let $q_p$ be the Tate period, $\tilde q_p=q_p/p^{\operatorname{ord}_p(q_p)}$, and let $\pi_\ell:G_p\to\operatorname{Syl}_\ell(G_p)$ be the Sylow projection. Let $R$ be the smallest subring of $\mathbb{Q}$ containing $\{\lambda(a,p)\}_{a\in G_p}$ and $\tau^{-1}$, where $\tau=\#E(\mathbb{Q})$ is finite, and define $S$ by $\ell\in S$ iff $\ell\mid\#G_p$ and $\ell^{-1}\notin R$. **Mazur–Tate's multiplicative refined BSD conjecture.** Then $\theta_p\in I(R,G_p)$ and, for every $\ell\in S$,

$$
\prod_{a\in G_p}\pi_\ell(a)^{\lambda(a,p)}\equiv\pi_\ell(\tilde q_p)^{\frac{\#\Sha_E\prod_{p'\in\mathcal{P}-\{p\}}C_{p'}}{\tau^2}}.
$$

This is the multiplicative reformulation of the refined Mazur–Tate conjecture for one split multiplicative prime; it is studied numerically in the source, with no resolution stated.

record.title: Torsion-corrected multiplicative Mazur–Tate conjecture
record.statement:
Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ have split multiplicative reduction at a prime $p$, put $G_p=\left(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\right)^*/\langle-1\rangle$, and let $\lambda(a,p)$ be the even modular symbol. Let $q_p$ be the Tate period and $\tilde q_p=q_p/p^{\operatorname{ord}_p(q_p)}$. Let $R$ be the smallest subring of $\mathbb{Q}$ containing $\lambda(0,1)/(2\operatorname{ord}_p(q_p))$, $\{\lambda(a,p)\}_{a\in G_p}$, and $(\#E(\mathbb{Q})_{\mathrm{Tor}})^{-1}$. Define $S$ by $\ell\in S$ iff $\ell\mid\#G_p$ and $\ell^{-1}\notin R$, and let $\pi_\ell$ be the Sylow projection. **Torsion-corrected multiplicative Mazur–Tate conjecture.** Then

$$
\sum_{a\in G_p}\lambda(a,p)=0,
$$

and for every $\ell\in S$,

$$
\prod_{a\in G_p}\pi_\ell(a)^{\lambda(a,p)}\equiv\pi_\ell(\tilde q_p)^{\frac{\lambda(0,1)}{2\operatorname{ord}_p(q_p)}}.
$$

If $\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb{Z}}E(\mathbb{Q})>0$, both sides are $1$. The paper proposes this torsion-corrected variation after numerical failures of the uncorrected conjecture; it reports supporting computations but no proof.

record.title: Revised asymptotic tiling conjecture for rigid spanning hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $r\ge 3$ and $1 \le s_1 \le \cdots \le s_r$ be integers, and let $m\coloneqq s_1+\cdots+s_r$. A spanning subgraph $F$ of $K_{s_1,\ldots,s_r}^{r}$ is **rigid** if, for some such integers with $v(F)=s_1+\cdots+s_r$, it satisfies $\tau_i(F)=s_1+\cdots+s_i$ for every $i\in [r-1]$, where $\tau_i(F)$ is the minimum size of a vertex set meeting every edge of $F$ in at least $i$ vertices. For integers $n\ge r$ and $1\le i\le r$, let $G_{n,i,\beta}(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$ be the $n$-vertex $r$-graph whose edges are the $r$-sets meeting a distinguished set of size $\lfloor\beta(s_1+\cdots+s_i)n\rfloor-1$ in at least $i$ vertices. **Revised tiling conjecture.** For every real number $\beta\in\left(0,\frac{1}{m}\right)$, 

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,\beta n \cdot F)=\max\left\\{|G_{n,i,\beta}(s_1,\ldots,s_r)|\colon i\in [r]\right\\}+o(n^r).
$$

The revision excludes the previously refuted formulation by imposing rigidity, a condition satisfied by complete multipartite hypergraphs and intended to capture the relevant covering-number obstructions. The source does not state a resolution.
